fact: Teminali OS is an autonomous AI studio that runs on your own machine: local models, local speech, local screen understanding.
Hosted providers are available and never required. Nothing has to leave the machine.
Teminali OS ships as a desktop application.
The product is Teminali OS. Frontier is the name of the routing gateway and the local model wrapper, not the product.
Frontier has three modes: Flash, Auto and Max. They are routing architectures over local engines, not models trained here.
Flash is a lightweight local model taking the whole task: instant edits, high throughput.
Auto is the adaptive router. It uses only qualified model paths and reports which path it selected.
Max is the heavyweight local model taking the whole task, and it is locked until its exact artifact qualifies.
The three modes pick a profile. They are not themselves models.
Claude Code and Codex run as the operator's own command-line tools in the real workspace.
No provider's flagship model is ever selected automatically.
In the voice stage one assistant speaks and another works: Temi holds the conversation, and the Teminali OS assistant does the engineering with no chat surface of its own.
While a run is in flight, asking what is going on is answered from that run rather than starting a second conversation. 'Stop' lands on the run; 'stop talking' stops only the voice.
The sidebar views are Chats, Explorer, Search, My Projects and Skills.
The workspace panel strip holds tabs of twelve kinds: File, Terminal, Browser, Canvas, Side chat, Guardian, Claude Code, Codex, Usage, Benchmark, Release and Video Editor.
Video Editor is the one panel limited to a single tab, because it owns a timeline and a playback clock that a second copy would compete for.
Search covers the whole application from one field: panels, skills, projects, workspace files by name and by content, chats, bookmarks, history and downloads.
The rail stays on screen when the sidebar panel is collapsed, so a dismissed sidebar is one click from open.
'The browser' means this application's own Browser panel, not Safari. A web address goes there unless another browser is named.
The screen assistant has three modes: dictate, talk and agent.
Its autonomy has three rungs: guide, confirm and auto.
The screen tools are look, click, type, key, scroll, drag, launch, focus and wait.
No screen tool takes a coordinate. Everything is aimed at something named on screen.
No terminal, Script Editor or Automator can be launched by the assistant: a shell prompt plus a type step is arbitrary code execution wearing an allowlist.
Opening an application is always the last step of a plan, because what it opens has no window to plan against yet.
Voice is local by default: whisper.cpp for recognition, and the system voice for speech.
Speech streams clause by clause, so a long reply starts speaking after its first clause rather than after all of it.
Nothing reaches the chat unreviewed: every spoken utterance passes a repair pass the operator sees before it sends.
Recognition and speech are routed independently, so upgrading one leaves the other where it was.
Guardian shows what the machine is holding right now.
In Guardian every number is measured or it is null. A metric that could not be read is never drawn as a plausible zero.
Guardian has three layers: a snapshot, an auto-unload that evicts idle resident models, and a governor that can close applications.
The governor quits an application gracefully and never by signal, never touches the app you are using, and treats unknown unsaved work as unsafe.
In the usage ledger an unreported cost is null, never zero.
In the benchmark arena the diff in the sandbox is ground truth; the transcript is only what the agent claims.
